## Writing the reference

The pages above are built from the javadoc in `src/`. A registered element or property has to carry
the tags the generator reads, and the build stops and names the class if one is missing:

```java
/**
 * One cell of a table. colspan and rowspan say how many of them it takes up.
 *
 * @ctml.group table
 * @ctml.properties colspan, rowspan
 * @ctml.example <td class="px-1 py-[2px]" colspan="2" text="diamond"></td>
 */
```

| Tag | On | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@ctml.group` | elements | Which heading the element reads under: root, layout, text, list, table, media, input |
| `@ctml.properties` | elements | The properties that do something on this element, or `none` |
| `@ctml.example` | elements, properties | One line of markup, shown as written |
| `@ctml.on` | properties | The elements that read the property |

Everything else is read off the code itself: an element's tag and whether it holds children come from
its constructor, the styles it starts with from the builder behind `defaultStyle()`, and the classes
that write a style from the registrations in `TailwindParser`.

Run it after changing any of them:

```bash
./docs/generate.sh
```
